evidence_summary: New Jersey business-directory data records Clark Music Industries with a January 26, 1968 registration date, providing a concrete legal/business anchor for the company during the East Coast Fuzz period.

A 1969 NAMM exhibitor list includes Clark Music Industries, Inc. alongside established musical-instrument manufacturers and distributors, confirming active participation in the U.S. music-products trade by that time.

A period trade advertisement places Clark Music Industries, Inc. at 61 Walnut Avenue, Clark, New Jersey 07066 and promotes its own audio products, establishing a documented commercial address and product-manufacturer/distributor presence.

A September/October 1968 classified-ad trail documented by Tone Machines places a used Clark Fuzz in circulation by October 5, 1968, proving the Clark-branded fuzz was already on the market by that date.

Former Clark employee Rich Excellente states that his work at Clark Electronics included assembling PA column speakers and wiring fuzz boxes. This is strong evidence of Clark facility involvement in fuzz production or final assembly, but does not by itself establish that Clark designed or populated every circuit.

entity: Clark SS-600 / East Coast Fuzz family
evidence_summary: Clark fuzz units carry an instruction label stating Manufactured and Distributed by Clark Music Industries. Combined with the employee testimony and company records, this makes Clark the strongest identified builder for its own branded state, while the broader East Coast Fuzz family still requires separate model-specific proof.

Rich Excellente reported that Clark supposedly built amp cabinets for Ampeg. Tone Machines notes the geographic proximity and narrative fit but explicitly says solid confirmation has not been located. Retain as a research lead only.

Tone Machines places the East Coast Fuzz family broadly in the New York/New Jersey area based on the locations of known branded states. This supports regional context only and does not identify a common factory.
